title: Best Transcription Services (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a transcriptionist for interviews, podcasts or meetings: accuracy, formats, confidentiality, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: Transcription turns audio and video into text, for interviews, research, podcasts, meetings and legal or medical records. Good transcripts are accurate, clearly formatted and delivered on time. They go wrong when automatic transcripts are delivered without review, speakers are not labeled, or confidential recordings are handled carelessly. This guide helps you order transcripts you can rely on.

faq.q: What is the difference between verbatim and clean verbatim?
faq.a: Verbatim includes every word, filler and false start. Clean verbatim removes ums, repeats and stutters while keeping the meaning. Most business and podcast transcripts use clean verbatim.
They are a useful start but often miss names, technical terms, accents and overlapping speech. Human review improves accuracy a lot.

faq.q: Can I get time stamps and speaker labels?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for speaker names and time stamps at regular intervals or at each speaker change.

faq.q: How do I protect confidential recordings?
faq.a: Share files through secure links you control, ask about storage and deletion, and use a confidentiality agreement for sensitive material.
Audio quality. Clear recordings with little background noise and one speaker at a time produce far better transcripts.
